A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Content can be matched reliably across pagination and figure-order changes.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices H–I report original speech-recognition experiments, including WER comparisons, optimizer and clipping ablations, and training with differential privacy.

after.justification: v3 retains the original LibriSpeech and Common Voice experiments, WER results, ablations, and differential-privacy evaluations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The transformer/CTC model, federated training procedure, server LAMB optimizer, local SGD, and global/uniform/dimension-based clipping methods are retained. Added optimizer descriptions clarify existing choices.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LibriSpeech and English, French, and German Common Voice coverage, including retained seed-model, domain-shift, IID/non-IID, and private-training scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 8–9 retain the same optimizer comparators within their respective experiments. The FedProx comparisons in Table 13 and centralized training baselines also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Data splits, preprocessing, WER evaluation, model sizes, cohort configurations, training budgets, and privacy-accounting procedures are retained. The newly stated LAMB stability constant does not establish a changed experimental setting.

E4.justification: Appendices H–I retain the architecture, optimizer, SpecAugment, seed-quality, cohort-size, clipping, and noise-placement analyses. No new or redesigned ablation, robustness study, or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Gradient and client-update plots retain their mean and standard-deviation reporting over clients/training steps. No repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: In Table 1, the no-noise row with C = 1 and cohort size 1,024 changes per-layer dev/test WER from 15.7%/18.9% to 15.9%/19.1%. The corresponding Table 17 row retains 15.7%/18.9%, creating an internal discrepancy. Other results are retained after matching relocated displays.

T1.justification: The bounds, assumptions, and derivations in Appendix F are retained. Added LAMB/SGD parentheticals and sampling-expectation descriptions restate choices and definitions already present in v2's proofs.

C1.justification: The benchmark contribution, role of per-layer clipping with adaptive normalization, and population-extrapolated privacy/utility claims remain unchanged, including the headline 1.3- and 4.6-percentage-point WER trade-offs.

C2.justification: Appendix I.3 newly explains that LAMB's xi = 10^-6 becomes a leading denominator term when clipping C < 10^-6. This adds numerical context to the retained observation that very small clipping thresholds do not affect performance.

D1.justification: v3's abstract adds a repository address and reports availability of all experiment and benchmark code; v2 only promises a future release. Appendix I.3 also newly discloses the LAMB stability constant xi = 10^-6.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are retained. Bibliography differences concern citation-page references rather than added literature or changed relationships to prior work.

P1.justification: Limited edits add optimizer and sampling clarifications, the code statement, a numerical-stability explanation, and acknowledgment changes. The section hierarchy and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is reduced in display size, and figures/tables shift with text reflow. Figure 3 moves earlier, while Figures 19–20 exchange order and numbering. The embedded graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added code location, disclosed LAMB constant, and clearer descriptions provide modest gains in reproducibility information and clarity. These gains are tempered by Appendix B's stale future-release wording and the revised Table 1 control now disagreeing with Table 17.
